questions.question: Do you need hearing protection on a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes, in addition to a helmet.
No, not if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, in addition to a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Hearing protection helps protect your ears while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, at what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person age 21 or older considered legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: A person of legal drinking age with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is considered legally intoxicated. It is illegal and unsafe to ride a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, how do they appear to other drivers?

options.text: They seem to be going faster than they really are.
They seem to be going slower than they really are.
They seem to not be moving when they really are.
They seem to be closer than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: They seem to be going faster than they really are.
questions.explanation: Because of their small size, motorcycles may appear to be traveling faster than they actually are.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, why should you not move to the far edge of your lane away from them?

options.text: It discourages them from cutting back into your lane too early.
It encourages them to cut back into your lane too early.
It encourages them to pass more quickly.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages them to cut back into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far edge of your lane when being passed is dangerous. It may encourage the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: What does swerving on a motorcycle require?

options.text: You should do it to avoid hazards on slippery roads.

questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick maneuver that needs a lot of traction to do safely. Do not make sudden moves like swerving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What lights should you use when riding in fog?

options.text: Switch between low and high beams.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use your high beams around other vehicles.

questions.question: How should you position yourself in your lane when going through a curve?

options.text: Stay in the same spot throughout the whole curve.
Always stay on the left side of the lane.
Always stay on the right side of the lane.
The best path may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best path may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to adjust your lane position as needed. The best path through a curve may not match the curve of the road itself.

questions.question: What should an effective face shield NOT be?
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be free of scratches, resist penetration, offer clear views on both sides, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. An airtight face shield can fog up and make it hard to see.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
The best position depends on the situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best position depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Choose a position that matches your current conditions, gives you enough space around you, and makes you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What is in the center of a lane?

options.text: It is always the safest place for a motorcycle.
It often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
It often has oil and grease, and is never safe for riding.
It is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this area usually has enough grip for safe riding. However, avoid large oil buildup spots, which are often found at busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: To stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly while gradually increasing the front brake pressure.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least four seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to work properly?

options.text: Block all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, permit air flow to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A helmeted rider is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and fastened securely or in saddlebags. Placing loads high on the back raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and changes its balance. Always distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the end of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This prevents them from falling behind and allows experienced riders to watch them.

questions.question: Which type of sign has a rectangular shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: In general, how many seconds should you stay behind another vehicle?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, why should you ride on the left side of your lane?

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
It gives you the best view of hazards in the next lane.
People don't expect to be passed on their left.
It puts you in the rearview mirror of the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you the best view of hazards in the next lane.
questions.explanation: Riding on the left side of your lane improves your view ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic when preparing to pass.

questions.question: The center of a lane usually has an oily strip. This area is:

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the middle of the lane. When the road is dry, this area gives motorcyclists enough grip to ride safely. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can ride to the side of it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: If you need to brake while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
Brake as hard as you would on a straightaway.
Wait until you are not in the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle is leaning than when it is upright. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake while turning, apply the brakes slowly and gently.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks at an angle, the safest way is to:
questions.explanation: The safest way to cross angled railroad tracks is to go straight in your lane. Turning to reach the tracks at a right angle is dangerous because it may force you into another lane.

questions.question: If you brake while in a curve:

options.text: It will be the same as braking on a straightaway.
You will have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. Some of the tire's grip is used to turn the motorcycle while leaning, so less grip is available for stopping.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire grips again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire grips again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever until the tire grips again, then re-apply the brake.
